subject: Saved Items step 1-2: Supabase tables + shared savedItems service
body:
Foundation for the shared "file manager" that any tool can use to save/open
its outputs into named items and folders.

- supabase/schema.sql: two new tables, ucc_folders (nestable via parent_id)
  and ucc_saved_items (tool_id + jsonb payload + folder_id), with indexes,
  updated_at triggers, and RLS + open anon policies matching the sync table.
  Foreign keys use ON DELETE SET NULL, so deleting a folder moves its items
  and subfolders to root instead of cascade-deleting them.
- src/shared/savedItems.ts: the shared service every tool calls. Since
  Supabase's PostgREST auto-exposes the tables at /rest/v1/*, this module IS
  the "backend endpoints" — listFolders/create/rename/move/deleteFolder and
  listItems/loadItem/createItem/rename/move/overwrite/deleteItem, mapping
  snake_case columns to camelCase and surfacing clear errors (not configured,
  auth, "run the SQL" on 404). List views omit the payload; loadItem fetches
  it for restoring a tool.
- tests: 14 cases covering mapping, filters (tool + folder/root), the
  move-into-itself guard, delete semantics, and the error hints.

Storage note: the app is a static site with no Node backend, so this builds on
Supabase (already wired for cloud sync) rather than a separate Express/Prisma
server — no new infrastructure to run.

  updated_at current. Much shorter, no functions to reason about.
- supabaseSync.ts: talks to the table's REST endpoint directly (GET/PATCH on

  and there's no passcode argument to thread through. Guard messages now

  seeded row can't be found.

- SettingsPage: removed the "Shared passcode" input; rewrote the warning
  banner to state the actual tradeoff plainly instead of describing a gate
  that no longer exists.

author: Claude
subject: Add cloud sync via Supabase: save/load the whole workspace across browsers
body:
Settings, generated timetables, and Module & Course Review data all live only
in this browser's localStorage — switching devices or browsers meant retyping
everything. This adds an optional "Cloud sync (Supabase)" section in Settings
to save/load the whole thing as one shared snapshot.

- supabaseSync.ts: snapshotLocalStorage() captures every "ucc*"-prefixed
  localStorage key (the app's full namespace) into a plain string map, with
  this browser's own Supabase connection fields (URL/Anon key/passcode)
  stripped out first — syncing those would be circular and would overwrite
  one browser's connection with another's. applySnapshot() writes a
  downloaded snapshot back, explicitly preserving THIS browser's connection
  fields since the incoming data never has them. testSupabaseConnection /
  saveToSupabase / loadFromSupabase call two Supabase RPC functions directly
  (no SDK needed — Supabase's REST API sends permissive CORS by design,
  unlike ERPNext) and distinguish "wrong passcode" from a real connection
  failure.
- supabase/schema.sql: one-time SQL for the user's Supabase project. A
  single-row table with Row Level Security enabled and NO policies (default
  deny for the anon role); the only way in or out is two SECURITY DEFINER
  functions that check a bcrypt-hashed passcode server-side before touching
  the row. The Anon/publishable key is not a secret (it ships in the public
  JS bundle) — the passcode check in Postgres is the real gate.
- SettingsPage: new "Cloud sync (Supabase)" section — Project URL, Anon key,
  shared passcode, a "Configured" status chip, and four actions: Save &
  reload, Test connection, Reload from Supabase, Clear (use local storage
  only). Save/Load both end in a page reload so every part of the app
  (settings, timetable, review planner, help/tour flags) re-reads its
  now-updated storage in one clean pass.
- settings.ts: three new local-only AppSettings fields (supabaseUrl,
  supabaseAnonKey, supabasePasscode).

New tests (14) cover snapshot/apply round-tripping (including the
connection-field-preservation case) and all three sync functions against a
mocked RPC endpoint (wrong passcode, empty-snapshot, network failure). 194
vitest pass; tsc/oxlint clean.

Verified against a local mock of the two Supabase RPC endpoints, full round
trip: wrong passcode rejected with a clear message; correct passcode
connects; loading before any save reports "nothing saved yet" instead of
silently succeeding; Save & reload survives with this browser's connection
fields intact; a simulated second browser (fresh localStorage, same
connection info re-entered) pulls the real data down via Reload from
Supabase; Clear empties only the three connection fields.

The production deploy builds with `vite build --base=/ucc_academic_hub/` so
assets resolve under that subfolder, but BrowserRouter had no matching

author: Claude
subject: Fix ERPNext CORS on deployed builds: always call same-origin /erp
body:
Symptom: on a deployed build (served at a plain origin, not the dev server),
"Test ERPNext connection" and "Load sample fields" failed with a CORS preflight
block — the browser called https://sms.unitedceres.edu.sg/... directly and the
ERPNext site returns no Access-Control-Allow-Origin header.

Root cause: erpBase() returned the raw base URL whenever import.meta.env.DEV was
false, so any production build fetched ERPNext cross-origin. The /erp same-origin
proxy only existed on the dev server, so only `npm run dev` ever worked.

Fix — the browser never calls ERPNext directly, in any mode:
- erpBase() now ALWAYS returns the same-origin '/erp' prefix (dev and build
  alike). Removed the now-dead trimBase helper.
- vite.config.ts applies the /erp proxy to BOTH server (dev) and preview
  (built app), so `npm run preview` behaves exactly like dev with no CORS.
  Factored the proxy into a shared erpProxy const; preview binds host:true.
- Updated the network-failure message and the Settings Base URL hint to explain
  the same-origin proxy and how to serve/repoint it (ERP_PROXY_TARGET); a bare
  static host must add its own /erp reverse proxy.
- erpBase test asserts the same-origin prefix in every mode and that the
  configured host never leaks into the request path.

Verified against a mock Frappe server (no CORS headers, like the real site) via
`vite build` + `vite preview`: Test connection returns "Connected as
n8n@email.com", Load sample fields loads COURSE-0001 and populates the mapping
dropdowns (child-table/link fields excluded); every request went same-origin to
/erp/api/... — zero direct calls to sms.unitedceres.edu.sg — and the secret
never appeared in a URL. tsc + oxlint clean, 176 vitest pass.

author: Claude
subject: Add Delivery Mode (Parallel/Series) to the Timetable generator
body:
Delivery Mode was in the data model but the schedule engine ignored it and
there was no way to pick it. This wires it end to end.

- courseEngine: generateCourseSchedule now branches on course.deliveryMode.
  * Parallel — each module's lessons land on CONSECUTIVE valid teaching days;
    when a module finishes before its end date, the next module is pulled
    forward to the next valid teaching day after the previous one ends (never
    earlier than its own start). No AL days.
  * Series — a module's lessons are spread EVENLY across its window and every
    valid teaching day strictly between two lessons becomes an AL (Autonomous
    Learning) buffer day. No AL before the first lesson, after the last, or on
    any blocked day; consecutive lessons produce none.
  New helpers: pickEvenlySpacedDates, nextValidTeachingDate, makeModuleAL
  (AL entries carry no teacher, room, or times and never conflict).

- DetailsFields: add the course-level Delivery Mode select (Parallel | Series),
  shared by the wizard and the full form.

- helpText: sharpen the Delivery Mode tooltip to the exact semantics.

- Tests: split the generation suite into Parallel and Series blocks and cover
  carry-over, "never pull earlier than own start", even-spread + AL fill,
  AL fields, no-AL-when-consecutive, and no-AL-on-blocked-days. 177 pass.

Verified in-app: Series shows AL rows and an AL-days count; Parallel shows
none; a manual amend that makes two modules share teacher + room + overlapping

subject: Timetable Generator: windowed scheduling, observed holidays, editable timetable
body:
Faithful rewrite per the amendment — the engine moves from month-anchored
auto-distribution to explicit per-module date windows.

1. Observed public holidays: a Singapore public holiday on a Sunday auto-blocks
   the following Monday ("<name> observed"). blockedDates now unions UCC +
   public + observed; nothing schedules on weekends or any blocked day. The
   preview shows an "Automatically observed" note.
2. Module Start/End Date: each module carries its own scheduling window (fields
   below Classroom). generateCourseSchedule places lessons on the EARLIEST valid
   teaching days within each module's window; lessons never fall outside it or
   on a blocked day.
3. Fit validation: validateModuleFit warns (non-blocking) when a module's
   available teaching days are fewer than its lessons, or a window is missing;
   only the days that fit are scheduled.
4. Conflict rule: a clash is flagged ONLY when two different modules share the
   same teacher AND overlapping time AND the same classroom on a date (class
   group no longer triggers it). Applies to generated and amended entries.
5. Manual amendment: a new "Amend" view makes every generated entry editable
   (date, times, teacher, classroom, module, lesson, activity); edits update the
   timetable immediately and re-run conflict detection.
6. Duplicate module: copies all fields into a new, independently-editable row.

Retired the now-incompatible month-anchored distribution, AL buffer days, and
the module-shift panel (manual editing supersedes shift); List/Calendar/Hybrid
views and exports keep working over the generated lessons. Start month and
delivery mode inputs removed from the form (kept on the type for imports).

subject: v5 step 5: module shift with end-of-month deadline guard
body:
- shiftModuleLater(lessons, moduleId, 1|2, holidays): every lesson in the
  module advances the chosen number of VALID teaching days (weekends and
  holidays are skipped as steps), order and lesson numbering preserved. The
  module's window months are fixed; in series mode its AL fill is rebuilt so
  vacated days become AL and consumed buffer days become lessons.
- Deadline guard: the module's last lesson must stay on or before the last
  valid teaching day of its final window month. A breaching shift is rejected
  with a warning naming the module and the deadline (DD MMMM YYYY), leaving
  the schedule untouched.
- Modules panel above the conflicts panel: per-module lesson count and span
  plus "Shift +1 day" / "+2 days" controls; conflicts re-scan after every
  applied shift.
- Series spread switched from the end-anchored round formula to an anchored
  floor stride (i*n/take): spacing stays roughly equal but the final lesson no
  longer sits ON the month's last valid day, leaving the trailing AL slack the
  shift feature consumes — with the old formula every series shift would have
  hit the deadline immediately and the feature could never apply.

deadline block naming the date, repeated shifts until blocked, parallel
blocks, other modules untouched) — suite 120 passing. Browser-verified:
